answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity with decay. Every agent locks a small slashable bond to transact — like a crystal lattice, the structure only holds when each node carries real weight. New identities start dim and earn trust over time, so a sybil farmer pays a linear cost per sock-puppet while honest agents compound reputation. Add challenges that arrive like a comet — unpredictable, brief, impossible to precompute at scale — plus periodic summits where sampled agents must defend their history live. Faking one identity is cheap; faking ten thousand is ruinous.
